newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MALDINI SAYS ITALY TAKING TOURNOI SERIOUSLY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MALDINI SAYS ITALY TAKING TOURNOI SERIOUSLY.

text.p: Italy could do without the four-nation Tournoi de France this week but since they agreed to take part they are determined to do their best, coach Cesare Maldini told a news conference on Monday.
"Its far from a friendly tournament, here if you don't get results there's always an outcry," he said of the matches against England, France and Brazil.
"It's not just a question of looking good. We must play determinedly in this tournament that we didn't want but that we find ourselves in and which we must honour."
"But it won't be easy because we're at the end of the season, many players are not right, we need a holiday."
Italy committed to playing the tournament under former federation head Antonio Matarrese, ousted from his job after the national team's poor showing at Euro '96.
To accommodate the tournament, the end of the Italian league season was brought forward with one day of matches being held in midweek last month. Serie A finished on Sunday.
"Brazil and England played recently, but I think they will have the same problems as us. We did not choose to play this tournament but we intend to do our best," said Maldini.

He said the matches would serve a useful purpose in enabling Italy to test replacements for defender Alessandro Costacurta and midfielder Demetrio Albertini, who will be suspended for the next World Cup qualifier against Georgia.

Maldini earlier called up veteran Juventus midfielder Attilio Lombardo as a late replacement for Piacenza's Eusebio Di Francesco, needed by his club for the serie A relegation playoff against Cagliari on June 14 or 15.
Roma-bound Di Francesco was the first Piacenza player to receive an international call.
Maldini said he called up Lombardo because, without Di Francesco, the side looked a bit short in midfield.
Albertini will also be unavailable for the last game against France because he is due to leave the squad after the game against Brazil on June 8 for a minor operation.
In defence, Maldini said his son Paolo was recovering from injury but would probably miss Italy's opening match.
Striker Alessandro Del Piero is also likely to be an early absentee having passed a late fitness test after being hit in the face by the ball during the European Cup final last week.
Team officials said Del Piero, who saw a specialist in Turin about the retina of his left eye, would be rested for two days as a precautionary measure.
Italy were flying to France later on Monday.
